reports.title: Richard Breatnach
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: NHS England will use this learning to inform its Digital Strategy. We will also include advice to General Practitioners about Special Patient Notes, which are used within the integrated urgent care software so alerts can be set up for NHS 111 call handlers and out of hours general practitioners when they access a particular patient record as part of the Pharmacy Urgent Medicines Supply service being introduced from 1st December 2016.
promises.summary: Develop digital alerts for patient records to prevent unsafe online prescribing

concerns.quote: Mr Breatnach (and anybody else) is able to apply online for medications
applying online, if the application form is not thoroughly checked , allows the applicant to lie or give false or misleading answers to critical questions which is what Mr Breatnach did
There was no evidence that the prescriber made any effort to contact Mr [name redacted] GP to find out if the answers that he gave were true

Prescribing Dihydrocodeine, a potentially addictive drug, used for the treatment of moderate to severe pain to a patient who the prescriber has never seen appears to fly in the face of good prescribing practice
The amount of Dihydrocodeine prescribed appears to be excessive
understand from the evidence that | heard at the Inquest that Dihydrocodeine should not be prescribed for migraine which is the reason Mr Breatnach gave for asking for this medication

reports.title: Jamie O'Connor: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: we expect pharmacy owners to: - Make sure that their website and the websites of companies they work with are arranged so that a person cannot choose a prescription only medicine and its quantity before there has been an appropriate consultation with a prescriber
promises.summary: Require websites to block prescription selection without prior prescriber consultation

promises.quote: we published updated guidance for doctors on prescribing in February 2021. This now places a greater emphasis on following the principles of good practice regardless of the medium through which a consultation is taking place, face to face or online.
promises.summary: Updated prescribing guidance emphasizes good practice across consultation mediums.

promises.quote: We are also aware that our regulatory partners, including MHRA and the GPhC, share our concerns about the lack of regulatory oversight in this area.
promises.summary: Collaborate with MHRA and GPhC to address regulatory gaps

promises.quote: The Department is working with other healthcare regulators including the General Medical Council and their equivalents in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in the area of digital healthcare provision. As a result, a review of the UK's legislative position was undertaken and gaps identified. These included cases involving inappropriate prescribing and a lack of checks with the patient's GP before prescribing.
promises.summary: Review UK legislation on inappropriate prescribing and lack of GP checks before prescribing

concerns.quote: There is no central tracking system or central database to record what each person has been prescribed and dispensed and by whom
There is no requirement to contact the GP of the person requesting drugs to let them know what has been prescribed
concerns.hazard: lack of GP awareness of prescribed medication

concerns.quote: There was no necessity for a face to face consultation with the person requesting the drugs and the prescriber before drugs were dispensed
There was a very limited questionnaire about the history of the person requesting the drugs
Persons requesting the drugs were able to ask specifically for which drug they wanted before contact with the prescriber
By virtue of where the company prescribing the drugs was registered there was limited regulation
